claims.text: Calibrated DSC can identify the melting or solidus temperature of high-entropy alloys from the sharp increase in heat capacity.
A combined DSC and dilatometry method can accurately determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change at melting.
The proposed combined method is suitable for high-throughput characterization across the HEA family.
At low temperatures, the heat capacity can be extrapolated toward 0 K using the Debye T^3 law.
At sufficiently high solid-state temperatures, heat capacity approaches the Dulong-Petit value of 3R when magnetic transitions and phase transformations are absent.
Heat capacity rises dramatically when the solidus temperature is reached.
Configurational entropy produces a vertical offset between thermal entropy and total entropy over the temperature range when phase-change contributions are absent.
Vibrational or phonon contributions establish the predictable solid-state heat-capacity baseline used in the analysis.
Integrating the DSC melting signal yields the latent heat and therefore the enthalpy of fusion.
A lever-rule-inspired analysis can be applied to the DSC data to extract latent heat.
The vertical difference between extrapolated thermal entropy and total entropy yields the entropy of fusion.
Concurrent dilatometry provides the volume change associated with melting.
The measurements can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties efficiently across a broad range of HEA compositions.
DSC-derived melting temperatures will agree with independent determinations to within ±5%.
Fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change will each be determined with accuracy similarly constrained to ±5%.
Magnetic transitions or additional phase transformations can complicate the heat-capacity signal and reduce applicability near melting.
Failure of heat capacity to follow standard Debye and Dulong-Petit behavior limits the proposed approach.
Traditional calorimetric and dilatometric methods for simple alloys often require separate, time-consuming experiments and may neglect configurational entropy in HEAs.
Extrapolation of low-temperature heat-capacity data and overlapping transitions introduce uncertainty into the extracted melting properties.

contradictions.description: The vertical entropy offset is identified as configurational entropy, but the mechanism then treats that same offset as the entropy of fusion. No liquid-solid entropy balance is supplied to reconcile these distinct quantities.

The design and rule call for independent comparison of melting temperature, enthalpy, entropy, and volume change, but the listed complementary measurement independently determines only melting temperature. Independent reference methods for the other three properties are not specified.
